Decision Statements
If statement - an If statement implements branching logic based on a testable condition.
Example: If Weather = Warm Then Go golfing Mow the lawn Sit on the porch Else Read a book Drink hot chocolate End If
So if the first condition was met, it will execute the action under it. If it is not, it will execute another block of action.
If Then ElseIf statement - The If Then ElseIf statement allows for an entire series of possible choices.
Example: If weather = very cold Then Wear a coat Elseif weather = chilly Then Wear a light jacket Elseif weather = windy Then Wear windbreaker Elseif weather = hot Then Wear no jacket End If
So there is an action that is going to be executed when one of the conditions was met.
If Then Else statement - executes an action if the condition is true, and executes an action if the condition is not true.
Example: If number = 1 Then MessageBox.Show("Your number is one") Else MessageBox.Show("Your number is not one") End If
Nested If statement - these are If statements within If statements. Any types of statement may be used inside a set of Then, Else, or Elseif statements of an If. - Nested If statements create more complex decision structure.
Example: If today = weekday Then if holiday = false Then MessageBox.Show("Today is a normal day.") Elseif holiday = true Then MessageBox.Show("Today is a special day.") End If End If
Select Case statement - similar to If Then ElseIf statement. It performs a series of tests, conditionally executes the first True condition.
Select Case is different in that: - a single test expression may be evaluated. - the test expression is listed once. - the possible values of the expression are then listed with their conditional statements
Case Else may be included and executed if none of the values match the expression.
Example: Select Case CInt (TextBox1.Text) Case 1 MessageBox1.Show("Day 1") Case 2 MessageBox.Show("Day 2") Case 3 MessageBox.Show("Day 3") Case Else MessageBox.Show("Day none") End Selecr
Rules in Decision Statements: - A block If statement must always end with an End If statement. - The keyword Then must appear on the same line as the word "If" - The keywords Else and End If must appear on lines by themselves. - The Else branch is optional. Only use an Else statement if there is a false branch. - Visual Basic automatically indents 4 spaces inside the True and False branches to make the statement easier to read.
